Either I'm really confused, or something's wrong with log entry turn values.
For example, in first test case we get the image with the following region:
```
  _
/ \
 / 
```
and this region in solution becomes:
```
 / 
/  
 \_
```
To me it is CW turn.
But the turn value in the input is -1, which according to statement means 1 turn CW.
So to undo the transformation, we need to actually do CCW turn instead, no?
Am I missing something?
Because I just turned all the regions in the same directions as the turn value.
Nice background image, although I don't see the point of duplicating puzzle name in the image.

* There are some test cases where the image width is not equal to w. You can verify this by adding the following code to the author's solution.

```
for i in range(h): assert len(grid[i]) == w, f"len(grid[i]) = {len(grid[i])}, w = {w}, i = {i}"
```

* There are some test cases where the square specified in the log goes out of the image boundaries. You can verify this by adding the following code to the author's solution.

```
assert 0 <= piv[0] - rad, f"piv[0] - rad = {piv[0] - rad}"
assert piv[0] + rad < h, f"piv[0] + rad = {piv[0] + rad}, h = {h}"
assert 0 <= piv[1] - rad, f"piv[1] - rad = {piv[1] - rad}"
assert piv[1] + rad < w, f"piv[1] + rad = {piv[1] + rad}, w = {w}"
```

* As suggested by @User123, please remove the "Graphs" tag. According to the definition at https://www.codingame.com/learn/graphs, the "Graphs" tag refers to graphs in graph theory.

Thank you.

Tried to solve the puzzle and got stuck on the first test: specifically, the last log "7 8 -23 2". If I understand correctly, this corresponds to a rotation made on a square centered at (7, 8) and with radius = 2 (or length = 5). However, this seems to exceed the height of the image since h = 10 but the rotated square contains (7, 8), (7, 9), and (7, 10). Am I missing something?

Quick comments first. I'll review this contribution and your other one in greater detail later.

Goal
* Please remove the leading spaces before "All Arts".

* Please move the log format and its explanation from the Input section to the Goal section.

* Please specify the coordinate system, including the directions in which the x- and y-coordinates increase, and the location of the origin (0, 0).

Input
* Please correct the following typos:

  • seperated => separated (twice)

  • represting => representing

Output
* Please add "<<[[h]] lines>>:" at the beginning.

* Please change "Completed" to "Reconstructed".

Constraints
* Please add a constraint for each input variable.

Stub generator
* Please change 1024 to match the upper bound used in the Constraints section.

Cover picture
* Please upload a cover picture for the puzzle.

Thanks.

Did all those. Please give it another look.
Thanks.

My Python code for reference:

from itertools import product

H, W = map(int, input().split())
L = int(input())
logs = input().split("  ")
grid = [list(input()) for _ in range(H)]

for log in reversed(logs):
    x, y, turn, radius = map(int, log.split())
    turn = (-turn) % 4
    R = radius * 2 + 1
    new_grid = [[""] * R for _ in range(R)]
    for c, r in product(range(R), repeat=2):
        nc, nr = ((c, r), (R - r - 1, c), (R - c - 1, R - r - 1), (r, R - c - 1))[turn]
        new_grid[nr][nc] = grid[y - radius + r][x - radius + c]
    for r in range(R):
        grid[y - radius + r][x - radius:x + radius + 1] = new_grid[r][:]

for row in grid:
    print(*row, sep="")
I honestly didn't think much about it at the time, so I just winged it. I'm open to any suggestions you might have

The log records the rotations performed during corruption, so -1 means the region was rotated 90° counterclockwise (not "1 turn CW"). I think there's just a small mix-up here. Have another look at that part of the statement and see if it clears things up!

I don't see any changes.
> A positive value indicates the number of 90° counterclockwise rotations, while a negative value indicates the number of 90° clockwise rotations.
> - turn = -1 (90° clockwise)
To me what you commented contradicts what is written in the statement.

You're right, I mixed up the directions in my earlier reply. Sorry for the confusion.

I think the issue lies here: "Because I just turned all the regions in the same directions as the turn value."

You actually figured out yourself when you said: "So to undo the transformation, we need to actually do CCW turn instead, no?"

So, should you turn all the regions in the same direction as the turn value?
I mean, I solved all the tests this way. Turning in the same direction instead of how I first understood the puzzle - undoing the corruption and turning in the opposite direction.

wow, this has been up for months and I never noticed it. In my mind, + was always clockwise and - counterclockwise, and my code followed that logic. I just messed up when writing the statement, which is why I was confused in my previous reply about why I'd written + as counterclockwise. Should've been more careful. I've changed it now. Thanks.
I'd replace puzzle name in the image with more sketches.

You're right, and thanks for pointing it out. This was my mistake—I accidentally swapped the meanings of the x- and y-coordinates in the statement. The sample and test cases were built assuming x increases from top to bottom (rows) and y increases from left to right (columns), while the statement described the opposite. I've corrected the statement to match the intended coordinate system. Thanks again for catching this!

Thank you for the clarification. Some comments from me:

[Goal]

- It might be helpful to give an example of what radius means, for example, "For example, a pivot point of (2, 4) with a radius of 2 contains points in the image with x-values between 0 and 4 (inclusive) and y-values between 2 and 6 (inclusive)."

- Not sure how I feel about explicitly telling players to reverse the diagnostic log to solve for the original image. Is there a way to just let the player infer how to process the diagnostic log for themselves?

- Please state that positive turn values are prepended with the "+" symbol. I am not sure if all languages will be able to parse "+1" into an integer.

- I would suggest to change x, y into r, c (or row, col) for clarity.

[Input]

- Please format line 3 as "[[diagnostic_log]], a string consisting of [[log_length]] log(s) separated by exactly {{2}} whitespaces. Each log adheres to the log format specified above."

[Constraints]

- Please specify constraints for the variables used in each log (i.e. x, y, turn, radius). For example, "[[radius]] ≤ [[x]] < [[h]] - [[radius]]" and "[[radius]] ≤ [[y]] < [[w]] - [[radius]]".

[Tags]

- Please add the ASCII Art and String manipulation tags, and remove the Graph tag :)

[Cases]

- Would love to see more cases if possible! In particular, all images are wider than they are long (i.e. their width is larger than their height). Please add some cases where the width and height are equal, or where the height of the image exceeds the width.

Thank you! :)

All sections
* Please change "log" to "entry" or "record", as it's confusing to describe both the whole log and its entries/records as logs.

* Then, in the Input section, please change "transformations" to "transformation [entries/records]".

* The constraints of x and y should be associated with h and w respectively, rather than w and h. However, changing the constraints means most cases violate the revised constraints. Similarly, in the Square Selection Example, the values of x and y seem to be swapped. Did you intend x and y to refer to row and column instead? Please fix all inconsistencies.

Goal
* Consider adding "undo the transformations," before "reconstruct and output" for clarity.

* Please add:
Each [entry/record] consists of 4 space-separated integers.
before "x y turn radius".

* Please move the coordinate system explanation ("The origin … to right.") to the explanation of (x, y).

* (x, y): Consider replacing "pivot point about which the rotation was applied" with "the [center/centre] of the rotated square" for simplicity.

* If the above point is adopted, please also replace other instances of "pivot point" with "center/centre".

* turn: Please add "is a signed integer with an explicit {{+}} or {{-}} sign. It" between "[[turn]]" and "indicates", and remove the entire paragraph about prefixes.

* turn: Please change "Positive value" to "A positive value".

* radius: Please change "frame" to "region".

* Square Selection Example: The example region consists of a row of entirely spaces, which aren't visible. Please revise the example for easier visualisation, e.g. choose a square region where every edge contains at least one visible character.

Constraints
* Please merge the first two constraints as:
0 < [[h]], [[w]] ≤ 50

  The original upper bounds (w: 45, h: 50) are close enough that merging them simplifies things with little impact.

* Please add a constraint on [[turn]] (consider restricting it to -100 and 100).

Cases
* Please add 2 new pairs (4 cases) at the start:

  (1) 1 transformation only

  (2) 2 transformations whose square regions partially overlap

  @User123 expressed uncertainty over whether to explicitly state that reconstructing the original image requires undoing the transformations in the reverse order of diagnostic_log. I think adding Pair 2 early would help players discover this themselves, removing the need for an explicit hint.

* Test 2 is the only case where the absolute value of one of the [[turn]]s exceeds 100 (+190). Please consider reducing it to 100 or below.

* +27 appears 3 times, +13 appears twice, -13 appears twice. Aside from +190, the absolute value of [[turn]] never exceeds 45. Please use more random [[turn]] values from the full range of -100 to 100.

* Currently, h < w in all but one case (where they're equal). Please:

  • balance the coverage by adding cases where h = w and h > w.

  • when adding cases, try not to mix portrait, landscape and square images within the same case pair.

Thanks.

Thanks again for all the feedback! I've gone through the statement and fixed the issues that were pointed out. Could you take another look? If you find anything else that could be improved, let me know.
Looks good, thank you for the changes! Just one last thing from me, please rename the test/validators to fix the numbering order. Thank you :)
